conventions.ordering: all list outputs in ascending id unless stated
conventions.what_this_fixture_is_for: The one state a conforming board cannot reach by posting: a `pins` edge to an id the log does not contain. 1.1.7 refuses it at the write path, so this arrives only by LOADING a log — a corrupted store, a partial restore, or a second implementation with a weaker write path. Every implementation has this branch and none of them can test it from their own transport, which is why it belongs here rather than in a server suite.
conventions.the_rule_under_test: 10.10 — a required document the log cannot resolve is STILL REQUIRED. The entry is reported with a null `ns`, never dropped. Dropping it silently shortens the canon set, which is exactly the failure 10.10 forbids: the reader is told their reading list is complete when it is not.
conventions.null_ns_is_normative: `ns` is null rather than omitted, and the entry keeps the same shape as a resolvable one, so a client iterating the set needs no branch. null must not render AS a namespace — a client printing it verbatim shows the reader the literal word, which is the client-side hazard this fixture exists to make testable.

checks._note: Envelope 3 is the CONTROL and is not decoration: a board that dropped the unresolvable entry would still serve a plausible one-item canon here, and only the pair distinguishes 'reported the gap' from 'quietly shortened the list'.

must_not: canon MUST NOT omit id 99 — a required document that cannot be resolved is still required (10.10)
unread MUST NOT omit id 99 — it has no ack, so it wants reading, and its unresolvability is not an ack
unread_count MUST NOT be 1 — a count that excludes what the list includes is worse than either alone
ns for id 99 MUST NOT be a string — inventing a namespace for an envelope the log does not have is a fabrication, not a default
the reduction MUST NOT raise — a dangling edge is a fact about the log, and a board that 500s here cannot report its own damage
